title: SecurityValidationPipelineMatrix
description: Productized, runner-neutral security validation pipeline matrix for Oyatie SCM/CI/CD. It defines the universal lane contract, evidence records, pass/fail policy, cadence, false-positive and VEX handling, and continuous-control evidence required before security validation can be claimed as mechanically enforced or production-ready.

_meta.source_request: REGSEC-002: define a productized universal pipeline matrix for chaos engineering, security scanners, SAST, DAST, IAST, BAS, automated pentesting, NIST SSDF, OWASP ASVS/SAMM/WSTG, SLSA, and existing oya-check supply-chain evidence without mutating product code or assuming a GitHub Actions north star.
_meta.claim_boundary: Planning/gate matrix only. This spec does not claim any lane is implemented, wired to branch protection, or production-ready. Mechanically-enforced claims require a Rust gate/controller, RED/GREEN fixtures, live required-context evidence, and audit-chain records per the claim contract.
related_decisions: ADR-0361 (superseded; retained only for license-vetted security-tool stack provenance)

non_negotiables: Pipeline lanes are product contracts, not one-off scripts or operator checklists.
The permanent contract is runner-neutral: the same canonical security validation matrix must execute under the live pipeline runner and any future owned runner without changing policy semantics.
No new oya CLI, shell, or local-only invocation can satisfy a blocking security-validation claim.
Candidate PR bytes are untrusted input; gate definitions, severity policy, exception policy, and allowlists come from trusted trunk/controller state.
Every blocking lane emits typed API evidence records and audit-chain references before it can contribute to a green aggregate status.
False-positive and VEX decisions are time-bound evidence records, never path-wide suppressions or comments in scanner output.
Secrets exposure is never VEXed; it requires removal, revocation/rotation evidence, and tenant/customer impact analysis.
BAS, security-chaos, and automated pen-test lanes must be safety-bounded and tenant-scoped before execution against shared or production-like environments.

runner_boundary.canonical_context: security-validation is a constituent of the one canonical pipeline aggregator; this matrix does not name a runner as the north star.
trusted_inputs: service inventory and tenant classification from trusted base
gate severity policy from trusted base
exception and VEX records from approved evidence stores
untrusted_inputs: candidate-generated scanner configuration unless explicitly allowlisted by trusted policy
allowed_execution_substrates: Rust gate binary or controller that normalizes scanner output into the evidence API
license-vetted scanner/tool adapter behind a product port
declarative policy-as-code bundle pinned by trusted digest
sandboxed dynamic-test environment with explicit tenant/cell blast radius
disallowed_execution_substrates: shell-only check treated as merge authority
local developer command treated as merge authority
proprietary SaaS scanner as the sole authoritative gate
scanner exit code without typed evidence normalization
candidate PR disabling or weakening its own gate

matrix_contract.aggregate_status_rule: The security-validation aggregate is green only when every applicable lane for the changed subject is pass, not_applicable_with_policy_reason, or waived_by_unexpired_approved_exception. Unknown applicability, missing evidence, stale evidence, duplicate lane records, and suppressions without evidence are red.

storage_and_access.write_path: security-validation evidence API owned by cloud-ci/security-validation control plane
storage_and_access.read_path: tenant-scoped evidence API plus audit-chain references; tenant admins only read their tenant evidence
storage_and_access.immutability: append-only records; correction records supersede prior records without mutation
storage_and_access.minimum_retention: per compliance pack; default 400 days for gate evidence and 7 years for regulated release/security-control evidence

requires: bounded asset/scope, never path-wide or repo-wide wildcard
owner and approver distinct from the author when severity is high or critical
component purl or immutable artifact digest
exploitability analysis tied to actual build/runtime configuration
expiry no later than the next release train or 30 days for critical exploited vulnerabilities
forbidden: VEX without component identity and vulnerability id

lane_groups.purpose: Fast deterministic pre-merge and nightly coverage over code, dependencies, secrets, and declarative infrastructure.
Image/file-system/package scanning, signatures, SBOM, provenance, and admission evidence for promotable artifacts.
Runtime and protocol validation against deployed or instrumented candidates.
Control-plane, detection, prevention, recovery, and fail-closed validation through bounded adversarial and fault-injection scenarios.
Ongoing evidence that controls remain present, fresh, effective, and tenant-scoped after merge and deployment.

security_validation_lanes.name: Static Application Security Testing

covers: source code for Rust, TypeScript/JavaScript, Python, policy code, and generated-code inputs
taint flows across request, tenant, policy, persistence, shell, file, network, and serialization boundaries
security-sensitive code paths including authn/authz, secrets, payments, DSR/privacy, cryptography, deserialization, and sandbox/tool invocation
scope.applicability: pre-merge for code and policy changes; nightly full-repo sweep; required pre-release for services with externally reachable or tenant-bound surfaces

cadence.pre_merge: changed-target and reverse-dependency SAST from trusted ruleset
cadence.nightly: full-repo SAST and rule drift scan
cadence.pre_release: full SAST for release candidate service set

blocks_when: critical finding of any confidence except explicitly refuted false positive
high-confidence high finding on authz, tenant isolation, secrets, injection, path traversal, SSRF, deserialization, sandbox escape, or command execution path
scanner/ruleset evidence missing, stale, or candidate-weakened
new nosec/allow suppression lacks approved exception record
warns_when: medium findings outside security-sensitive surfaces with owner and remediation SLA
pass_requires: exception refs for every suppressed blocking finding

requires: refutation evidence tied to the current revision

standards_mapping: NIST SSDF: secure implementation and vulnerability review practices
OWASP ASVS: application control verification categories
OWASP SAMM: implementation and verification streams
productization_requirements: Repo-owned ruleset bundle versioned independently of candidate PR bytes
Adapter output normalized by Rust security-validation gate
Tenant/security-sensitive path classifier maintained as trusted policy data

security_validation_lanes.name: Dynamic Application Security Testing

covers: running web/API surfaces in isolated preview, staging, canary, or release-candidate environments
authentication, authorization, session, input validation, browser/API behavior, headers, TLS, and common web attack classes
tenant-bound routes and compliance-pack overlays
scope.applicability: pre-release for externally reachable services; nightly or weekly against stable preprod; post-deploy canary for high-risk internet-facing changes

cadence.pre_release: authenticated and unauthenticated scan of service candidate
cadence.scheduled: weekly full scan and nightly smoke scan for internet-facing surfaces
cadence.post_deploy: bounded canary scan on newly promoted endpoints

blocks_when: critical or high exploitable vulnerability is confirmed
auth bypass, tenant data exposure, SSRF to internal metadata/control plane, injection, or unsafe file access is detected
target inventory or credential fixture missing for an applicable service
scanner cannot prove it reached the intended deployment target
warns_when: low/medium hardening findings with remediation owner and SLA

requires: request/response replay evidence or controlled manual retest

standards_mapping: OWASP WSTG: dynamic test methodology
OWASP ASVS: verification categories for web/API controls
NIST SSDF: vulnerability verification and response evidence
productization_requirements: DAST targets are provisioned through tenant-scoped preview/staging environments
Credentials and seed data come from OpenBao/test-fixture authority, not candidate code
Results link to service inventory and exposure classification

security_validation_lanes.name: Interactive Application Security Testing

covers: instrumented application/API runtime during integration and end-to-end tests
runtime data flows, library calls, unsafe deserialization, injection, crypto misuse, and authz boundary violations
test personas and fixtures exercising tenant, compliance-pack, and policy domains
scope.applicability: pre-release for services with runtime instrumentation support; nightly for high-risk services; required before production-ready claim for internet-facing services

cadence.nightly: instrumented smoke/regression suite for high-risk surfaces
cadence.on_demand: security reviewer-triggered run for auth, secrets, DSR/privacy, sandbox, or payment changes

blocks_when: confirmed runtime exploit path with high or critical severity
authz/tenant isolation violation is observed
instrumentation coverage is below lane policy for the changed service
runtime evidence is missing for a claimed IAST gate
warns_when: coverage gap outside changed/high-risk paths with owner and next-run SLA

standards_mapping: NIST SSDF: verification with tool-based analysis and regression evidence
OWASP ASVS: runtime verification of application controls
OWASP SAMM: verification practice maturity
productization_requirements: IAST agents/adapters run only in approved test environments unless explicitly risk-accepted
Runtime traces are redacted and tenant-scoped before evidence publication
Coverage policy is machine-readable per service class

security_validation_lanes.name: Software Composition Analysis

covers: Cargo.lock, package manifests, container package inventories, vendored tools, build plugins, generated SBOMs, and transitive dependency metadata
vulnerability databases, license allow/deny policy, dependency maturity, stale direct dependencies, and known-exploited vulnerability overlays
existing check-supply-chain evidence fields for cargo-deny, cargo-audit, Trivy/osv, SBOM, Cosign/Rekor, and provenance posture
scope.applicability: pre-merge for dependency/lockfile/build-tool changes; nightly for vulnerability database drift; release for artifact SBOM and provenance

cadence.pre_merge: changed dependency graph and policy diff
cadence.nightly: full graph re-scan against fresh vulnerability/license intelligence

blocks_when: forbidden license appears without ADR-approved exception
critical/high vulnerability is reachable/exploitable without unexpired VEX or fixed version path
known-exploited vulnerability lacks fix, mitigation, or approved short-lived exception
SBOM/provenance/signature evidence is missing for release artifacts
dependency scanner evidence is stale or candidate-weakened
warns_when: medium vulnerability with owner/SLA and no known exploitation
dependency freshness advisory outside release path
pass_requires: VEX/exception refs for non-fixed blocking vulns

requires: OpenVEX or CSAF VEX record for component vulnerabilities
component purl or immutable artifact digest
exploitability analysis tied to actual build/runtime config
expiry <= 30 days for critical known-exploited vulnerabilities

standards_mapping: NIST SSDF: third-party component and vulnerability response practices
SLSA: source/build/provenance tracks
OWASP SAMM: implementation/dependency management maturity
productization_requirements: Reuses and extends check-supply-chain evidence concepts instead of duplicating supply-chain policy
SBOM and provenance records are immutable release artifacts
VEX decisions are API records, not scanner inline suppressions

security_validation_lanes.name: Secret and Credential Exposure Detection

covers: source diffs, full tracked history windows, config, IaC, container layers, logs/evidence bundles, notebooks, fixtures, and generated artifacts where applicable
tokens, private keys, passwords, cloud credentials, signing materials, webhook secrets, database URLs, and high-entropy credential-shaped strings
secret reference policy such as sref:// OpenBao references without raw secret bytes
scope.applicability: every pre-merge change, every release artifact, and scheduled full-history rescans after rule updates

cadence.pre_merge: diff and changed-file scan before merge
cadence.nightly: full tracked corpus and evidence/log redaction scan

blocks_when: verified credential or secret material is present
credential-shaped finding cannot be classified before merge
raw secret bytes appear where only sref:// or sealed refs are allowed
revocation/rotation evidence is missing for confirmed exposure
warns_when: low-confidence high-entropy string is refuted and recorded with a short recheck SLA
pass_requires: secret scanner version and ruleset digest

requires: evidence that the value is not a credential

standards_mapping: NIST SSDF: protect source and credentials used by the build/deployment process
OWASP ASVS: secret management and credential storage controls
SLSA: build and provenance integrity requiring protected credentials
productization_requirements: Findings are always redacted in evidence API responses
Confirmed exposure opens a rotation workflow, not merely a lint failure
sref:// and sealed-reference patterns are treated as allowlisted references, not secrets

security_validation_lanes.name: Infrastructure-as-Code and Policy-as-Code Security

covers: OpenTofu/Terraform, Kubernetes YAML, Helm/Kustomize manifests, Argo CD app manifests, NetworkPolicy, Pod Security, Kubewarden/Kyverno policy, Cedar policy, cloud resource specs, and branch/protection declarative state
public exposure, encryption, IAM, service account, network egress, tenant isolation, drift, admission, and breakglass controls
scope.applicability: pre-merge for infrastructure/policy/config changes; deploy-time for rendered manifests; scheduled drift/control scan

cadence.pre_merge: static IaC and policy scan over changed declarative assets and rendered plans where available
cadence.deploy_time: admission/policy evaluation of rendered manifests and plans

blocks_when: public exposure, broad IAM/admin role, wildcard secret access, or unencrypted storage appears without approved exception
tenant isolation, network policy, pod security, or admission policy is weakened
policy code fails default-deny or deny-overrides-permit invariants
rendered plan evidence is missing for applicable deploy-time resource changes

standards_mapping: NIST SSDF: secure configuration and infrastructure evidence
OWASP SAMM: design and operations control maturity
OWASP ASVS: deployment and configuration verification controls
productization_requirements: IaC scanners run against source and rendered artifacts where rendering is deterministic
Admission policy engines provide deploy-time evidence consumed by the same security-validation API
Exceptions must name specific resources and cannot suppress an entire IaC directory

security_validation_lanes.name: Container, Image, and Artifact Security

covers: Dockerfiles/Containerfiles, base images, OS packages, language packages, filesystem layers, image metadata, runtime user/capabilities, SBOMs, signatures, provenance, and admission verifier records
release artifacts and deployable OCI images for every service/cell/tenant tier
scope.applicability: build and promotion for deployable artifacts; nightly re-scan of retained images; deploy-time admission verification

cadence.build_time: filesystem/container scan and SBOM generation for every promotable artifact
cadence.nightly: retained image re-scan against updated vulnerability data

blocks_when: critical/high exploitable vulnerability lacks fixed version, mitigation, or unexpired VEX
image runs as root or carries forbidden capabilities without exception
base image is unpinned, unapproved, end-of-life, or license-forbidden
SBOM, signature, Rekor/transparency, provenance, or admission record missing for release/promotion
runtime hardening policy is weakened
warns_when: medium vulnerability with owner/SLA and no known exploitation
pass_requires: VEX/exception refs for remaining blocking vulnerabilities

requires: expiry <= 30 days for critical/high release blockers

standards_mapping: SLSA: artifact provenance and build integrity
NIST SSDF: release integrity and vulnerability response
OWASP SAMM: operations/deployment assurance
productization_requirements: Integrates with check-supply-chain release evidence fields
Admission verifier records are required for deployment, not optional release notes
Re-scans can turn a previously passing image red when fresh vulnerability intelligence changes risk

security_validation_lanes.name: Implementation Fuzzing

covers: parsers, serializers/deserializers, protocol handlers, policy parsers, cryptographic envelope handling, document/markdown parsers, webhook/event decoders, and any boundary accepting untrusted bytes
memory safety, panics, hangs, resource exhaustion, differential behavior, and sanitizer findings where supported
scope.applicability: nightly for fuzz target corpus; pre-merge smoke for changed fuzz-covered targets; pre-release for security-sensitive parsers/protocols

cadence.pre_merge: bounded changed-target fuzz smoke with corpus regression replay
cadence.nightly: time-budgeted fuzz campaign and corpus minimization
cadence.pre_release: extended fuzz budget for security-sensitive changed components

blocks_when: new crash, panic, sanitizer violation, data corruption, infinite loop, or excessive memory/CPU case is found
known crashing corpus input is not replayed in regression tests
fuzz target coverage drops for a boundary classified as untrusted input
warns_when: coverage growth stalls below target without new crash for non-critical boundary
pass_requires: crash artifact refs or no-crash statement

requires: root-cause note proving non-security or unreachable condition

standards_mapping: NIST SSDF: test executable code and prevent recurring vulnerabilities
OWASP SAMM: verification depth and security regression testing
productization_requirements: Every untrusted-byte parser has an owner and fuzz-target applicability row
Crash artifacts are stored in restricted evidence with sanitized metadata exposed through the API
Fixes add corpus regression replay before the finding can close

security_validation_lanes.name: API Contract and Protocol Fuzzing

covers: OpenAPI, AsyncAPI, gRPC/proto, GraphQL, webhook, event, and internal service boundary contracts
schema validity, negative inputs, auth persona permutations, tenant context confusion, rate-limit/quotas, idempotency, and error-shape invariants
scope.applicability: pre-release for API contract changes and internet/tenant-facing APIs; nightly against stable preprod contracts; pre-merge smoke for high-risk schema changes

cadence.pre_merge: schema-derived negative smoke for changed contracts
cadence.pre_release: auth-aware, tenant-aware fuzz campaign against candidate environment
cadence.nightly: full contract fuzz against stable preprod

blocks_when: authz bypass, tenant escape, privilege confusion, rate-limit bypass, unsafe state mutation, or schema-inconsistent success is detected
unexpected 5xx or panic occurs for generated valid/invalid inputs above policy threshold
contract or environment evidence is missing for an applicable API surface

requires: auth persona and tenant fixture id

standards_mapping: OWASP ASVS: API and access-control verification
OWASP WSTG: dynamic test methodology
NIST SSDF: security testing and vulnerability response
productization_requirements: Contract fuzzing consumes API contracts as product inputs, not hand-written ad hoc curl scripts
Tenant/persona fixtures are centrally governed
Replay artifacts are stable enough for developer reproduction and auditor evidence

security_validation_lanes.name: Breach and Attack Simulation / Purple-Team Validation

covers: bounded MITRE ATT&CK-style adversary emulation scenarios for identity, secrets, lateral movement, exfiltration, persistence, CI/CD abuse, cloud control plane abuse, and tenant-isolation attempts
expected prevention, detection, alerting, audit-chain, response, and recovery controls
blue-team and purple-team evidence showing which control observed or stopped the scenario
scope.applicability: monthly/quarterly for high-risk control sets; before production-ready claim for regulated or internet-facing services; after major identity/network/security-control changes

cadence.quarterly: full purple-team scenario pack for regulated and internet-facing systems
cadence.pre_release: targeted scenario pack for high-risk security-control changes

blocks_when: required prevention or detection control fails for a scenario classified release-blocking
scenario produces cross-tenant access, secret disclosure, policy bypass, or unlogged privileged action
expected alert/audit evidence is absent or stale
scenario blast-radius controls are missing
warns_when: detection latency or enrichment misses target but no prevention/control failure occurs

risk_acceptance_required_when: scenario cannot be safely run before release

standards_mapping: NIST SSDF: verify and respond; reduce recurrence through controls
OWASP SAMM: operations and verification maturity
OWASP ASVS: defense-in-depth control validation
productization_requirements: BAS scenarios are cataloged, versioned, and safe-by-default
Control evidence joins to continuous-control snapshots
Purple-team verdicts are evidence records, not meeting notes

security_validation_lanes.name: Security Chaos Engineering

covers: bounded fault injection into identity provider, PDP/policy engine, audit-chain sink, secrets/KMS, signing/provenance, admission controller, network policy, rate-limit, and detection pipeline dependencies
fail-closed behavior, degraded-mode policy, control-plane recovery, tenant isolation under partial failure, and audit continuity
scope.applicability: quarterly for critical control planes; pre-release for changes touching identity, policy, audit, secrets, signing, admission, or tenant isolation; post-incident regression

cadence.pre_release: targeted chaos scenario for changed security-control dependency
cadence.post_incident: regression scenario matching incident failure mode

blocks_when: system fails open when a security dependency degrades
tenant isolation, policy enforcement, audit emission, or secret protection is bypassed during fault
rollback/recovery evidence is missing for release-blocking scenario
blast-radius controls or abort criteria are missing
warns_when: recovery objective missed without security bypass and with approved remediation plan

requires: proof that observed behavior is safe and expected
risk_acceptance_required_when: release proceeds with a known fail-open or missing-audit behavior

standards_mapping: NIST SSDF: verify security requirements and prevent recurrence
OWASP SAMM: operations/control validation maturity
Hyperscaler readiness: chaos/fault-injection evidence for production/hyperscaler claims
productization_requirements: Security chaos scenarios are declared as data and executed by a controller with abort semantics
Production-like execution requires tenant/cell allowlist and blast-radius approval
Fail-open behavior is red unless explicitly approved as a bounded risk exception

security_validation_lanes.name: Automated Penetration Test and Exploit-Chain Validation

covers: automated exploit-chain tests across web/API/business logic/authz/tenant boundaries using safe payloads and replayable scenarios
internet-facing, regulated, tenant-admin, privileged operator, and CI/CD control-plane surfaces
abuse cases that require multi-step setup rather than single scanner findings
scope.applicability: pre-release for internet-facing or regulated service changes; quarterly for high-risk surfaces; before production-ready or hyperscaler-grade claim

cadence.pre_release: targeted scenario pack for changed/high-risk surfaces
cadence.on_demand: security reviewer triggered run for major authz/tenant/security changes

blocks_when: verified high/critical exploit chain succeeds
tenant escape, privilege escalation, data exfiltration, unsafe state mutation, or CI/CD control-plane abuse succeeds
test harness cannot prove safe target and payload boundaries
manual-only pen-test claim lacks API evidence record
warns_when: low/medium abuse path requires unrealistic preconditions but remains owner-tracked

standards_mapping: OWASP WSTG: penetration-test family coverage
OWASP ASVS: application and API control verification
NIST SSDF: vulnerability verification and response
productization_requirements: Automated pen-test packs are versioned product assets and can be rerun by the pipeline
Scenarios use safe payloads and do not rely on uncontrolled third-party targets
Manual analyst notes can enrich but cannot replace typed evidence records

security_validation_lanes.name: Continuous Control Evidence and Compliance Drift

covers: runtime and post-deploy evidence that required security controls remain present, configured, fresh, tenant-scoped, and effective
mTLS, service mesh, PDP/Cedar, admission policy, audit-chain, logging/alerting, secret lease/rotation, image admission, branch/protection, SLO/security alert, and compliance-pack controls
control snapshots for tenant-facing service claims and regulated pack obligations
scope.applicability: continuous for deployed control planes and tenant-facing services; daily snapshot for release posture; required before production-ready/hyperscaler security claims

cadence.continuous: control event stream and drift detector
cadence.daily: signed posture snapshot for each service/cell/tenant tier
cadence.release: snapshot pinned to release evidence packet
cadence.post_deploy: canary/ring control confirmation before wider promotion

blocks_when: required control evidence is missing, stale, unsigned, or not tenant-scoped
control drift weakens authz, tenant isolation, secrets, audit, admission, or image provenance
release packet cites a control snapshot older than policy allows
security exception expires without renewal or remediation
warns_when: non-release posture degradation has owner/SLA and does not weaken a blocking control

requires: compensating control or corrected inventory evidence
risk_acceptance_required_when: required runtime control is absent or stale for a release or production-ready claim

standards_mapping: NIST SSDF: ongoing vulnerability response and secure operations evidence
OWASP SAMM: operations and governance maturity
SLSA: continuous provenance and artifact integrity evidence where controls cover build/release
productization_requirements: Control evidence is produced continuously, not assembled manually at release time
Snapshots are tenant/cell/service scoped and queryable by evidence API
Freshness and exception expiry are enforced by the aggregate security-validation status

minimum_lane_applicability.when: dependency manifest, lockfile, build tooling, vendored code, or release artifact changes
IaC, policy-as-code, branch protection, admission, network, identity, or secret configuration changes
API/webhook/event contract or tenant-facing API behavior changes
untrusted-byte parser, protocol decoder, document parser, or sandbox/tool boundary changes
identity, policy, audit, secrets, admission, CI/CD, or tenant-isolation control changes
production-ready, hyperscaler-grade, secure, isolated, or regulated release claim is made

product_api_surface.purpose: Target API record shapes for the security-validation product surface. This section is a contract target only; it does not implement endpoints.
product_api_surface.tenant_isolation: Every API resource carries tenant_id and service/cell scope. Cross-tenant reads are denied by default; Oyatie internal dogfood runs use tenant_id=oyatie-internal without privileged sharing.
product_api_surface.audit_chain: Every create/update/supersede action emits an audit-chain event with actor, producer_identity, trusted timestamp, subject, result, exception refs, and previous_record_ref when applicable.

initial_gate_catalog_targets.purpose: Validate this matrix has all required lane ids and required row fields.
initial_gate_catalog_targets.promotion_target: blocking before any security-validation aggregate can claim mechanical enforcement

initial_gate_catalog_targets.purpose: Validate lane result/finding/exception/VEX/control snapshot records before the aggregate status consumes them.
fixtures_required: good lane result with typed evidence

initial_gate_catalog_targets.purpose: Map changed subjects and service classifiers to required lanes, refusing unknown applicability as false green.
fixtures_required: good API contract change requiring api_fuzzing+dast+iast
bad production-ready claim without all 13 lanes
bad IaC change missing continuous-control evidence

known_gaps_before_green: No Rust validator/gate is added by this planning matrix task.
No fixtures are added by this task; fixture rows above are target contracts for follow-up gate implementation.
Existing check-supply-chain covers a subset of SCA/container/release evidence but does not cover the full universal security-validation matrix.
BAS, security-chaos, automated pen-test, DAST, IAST, fuzzing, and API fuzzing require safe sandbox/preview environment contracts before any live execution claim.
Continuous-control evidence requires runtime control inventory and trusted-clock freshness before it can block release or production-ready claims.
